## Summary

**Data source overview.** This paper ("Safe Reinforcement Learning with Model Uncertainty Estimates") develops a Safe RL framework for dynamic pedestrian/obstacle collision avoidance in which an ensemble of LSTM collision-prediction networks, trained with bootstrapping and evaluated with Monte Carlo Dropout, produces per-motion-primitive mean and variance collision probabilities. A model predictive controller penalizes predictive variance so the agent regionally and gradually avoids novel (out-of-distribution) observations, and an increasing variance penalty schedule is used to aid exploration during training. Experiments in a 1D toy case and a gym-based multi-dimensional simulation show regionally elevated uncertainty in four novel scenarios and fewer collisions than an uncertainty-unaware baseline.

**EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]** — The paper has an unusually clean risk → problem → insight → design → mechanism → evidence → intervention structure, so the fabric maps well. Residual uncertainty comes from (a) the paper stating no explicit "interventions" (all intervention nodes are moderate-inference re-castings of the proposed method components, which is standard for a methods paper), and (b) edge-verb semantics: the canonical list is mostly problem-oriented (caused_by, mitigated_by), while insight→design and mechanism→evidence transitions in an engineering paper are better described by "enables"/"is realized by". *Instruction improvements that would help:* (1) explicitly define whether edge verbs read source→verb→target or target→verb→source (the template implies the former but "mitigated_by" from insight to design reads backwards); (2) provide guidance on how to encode *negative/limiting* validation evidence (here: dropout overconfidence, uncollaborative agents not flagged) that motivates future-work interventions; (3) clarify how to represent "rejected alternative approaches" (reachability analysis, safety-controller switching, model-free Q-uncertainty, Bayesian NNs) — I encoded these as problem-analysis nodes feeding the enabling insights; (4) allow an explicit "future work / research agenda" intervention maturity flag.

**Inference strategy justification.** Moderate inference was used to (i) convert the paper's methodological contributions into deployable intervention nodes (marked maturity 1–2, edge confidence 1–2 where inference dominates), (ii) attach the "rejected alternatives" critique from Related Work into the causal chain as problem analyses addressed by the regional-uncertainty insight, and (iii) create the feedback link from the variance-penalty design rationale to the exploration-suppression problem (explicitly discussed in III-D, so confidence 3).

**Extraction completeness.** 34 nodes (2 risk, 8 problem analysis, 5 theoretical insight, 5 design rationale, 7 implementation mechanism, 7 validation evidence) and 6 interventions, with 52 edges. All framework components (LSTM ensemble, MC-Dropout, bootstrapping, MPC cost, adaptive λv, masking, on-policy dataset collection) are decomposed as white-box nodes rather than a single "Safe RL framework" node. All quantitative results (Table I values, 32 ms inference, 80% collision local minimum) are captured in validation-evidence node descriptions.

**Key limitations.** Simulation-only, single-obstacle validation; no real-robot deployment; the negative calibration result (V-A) limits the strength of the epistemic-uncertainty-as-novelty-detector claim; collision-count improvements are reported graphically (Fig. 6) without statistical tests, capping several edge confidences at 3–4.
